questions.title: URL Shortener Service
questions.description: Design a URL shortener service that maps long URLs to short aliases. The system must optimize for extremely high read throughput (redirects) while minimizing database load.
requirements: Ensure persistent storage of URL mappings
expectedPatterns: Uses caching to bypass database for frequent redirects
Scales read nodes horizontally behind a load balancer
antiPatterns: Querying the primary database for every redirect request
Single point of failure in the routing layer
idealSolutionCharacteristics: Places a Redis/Memcached layer in front of the DB for fast short-code resolution
Uses horizontal scaling for redirect servers

questions.title: Basic Key-Value Store
questions.description: Design a simple distributed key-value store. Focus on data partitioning to handle datasets larger than a single machine's memory, ensuring balanced load.
expectedPatterns: Horizontally partitions data across multiple shards
antiPatterns: Storing all data on a single monolithic database instance
Failing to replicate shards for redundancy
idealSolutionCharacteristics: Implements consistent hashing to distribute keys across shards
Replicates data to prevent loss on node failure

questions.title: API Gateway Rate Limiter
questions.description: Design a centralized rate limiter for an API Gateway. The system must enforce quotas strictly with minimal latency penalty to the underlying APIs.
requirements: Add no more than 15ms latency per request
expectedPatterns: Uses an in-memory cache for fast quota lookups and decrements
antiPatterns: Using a disk-backed relational DB for every token check
Synchronous locks causing request queuing
idealSolutionCharacteristics: Implements a Token Bucket or Sliding Window algorithm using Redis
Executes atomic operations (e.g., Lua scripts) in cache to prevent race conditions

questions.title: User Authentication Service
questions.description: Design a centralized authentication service. The service must issue and validate session tokens securely while remaining highly available.
requirements: Maintain token validation p95 latency under 30ms
expectedPatterns: Caches active session tokens to avoid hitting the identity DB
Load balances stateless auth servers
antiPatterns: Stateful authentication servers storing sessions in local memory
Querying user DB for password hashes on every API request
idealSolutionCharacteristics: Uses stateless JWTs or an external distributed cache for session IDs
Decouples read-heavy validation from write-heavy login/registration

questions.title: Email Notification Dispatcher
questions.description: Design a system to send high volumes of transactional emails. The ingestion API must return quickly, while actual sending occurs reliably in the background.
requirements: Ensure 0% message loss for accepted requests
expectedPatterns: Uses a message broker to decouple API from slow external email providers
antiPatterns: Synchronously waiting for the SMTP server to respond before returning API success
Keeping notification state only in application memory
idealSolutionCharacteristics: API nodes write directly to a durable message queue (e.g., RabbitMQ, Kafka)
Worker nodes consume from the queue to dispatch emails, handling retries asynchronously

questions.title: Image Thumbnail Generator
questions.description: Design a compute-heavy service that generates thumbnails for uploaded images. The design must prevent large image uploads from blocking thumbnail generation resources.
requirements: Isolate upload logic from CPU-intensive resizing
expectedPatterns: Offloads compute-intensive resizing to background workers via a queue
antiPatterns: Processing image resizing synchronously on the web server
Storing binary image data directly in a relational database
idealSolutionCharacteristics: Upload API writes original image to Object Storage and drops an event in a Queue
Worker fleet processes the queue, generates thumbnails, and saves them to Object Storage

questions.title: Health Check Status Page
questions.description: Design a status page backend that ingests health pings from thousands of microservices and serves aggregated status overviews to dashboards.
requirements: Serve dashboard views with p95 latency under 100ms
Retain 7 days of historical uptime data
expectedPatterns: Uses an optimized write path for telemetry data
Caches pre-aggregated status states for dashboard reads
antiPatterns: Running heavy GROUP BY queries on relational DB for every dashboard load
Dropping health checks during traffic spikes
idealSolutionCharacteristics: Uses a Time-Series Database (TSDB) for efficient high-volume writes
Caches the current 'global status' to serve read requests instantly

questions.title: Pastebin Text Sharing
questions.description: Design a text sharing service where users create snippets of text that are assigned a unique URL. Focus on a write-once, read-many architecture.
requirements: Handle 500 writes and 5000 reads per second
Store data reliably with high availability
expectedPatterns: Caches text blobs heavily to serve viral pastes directly from memory
antiPatterns: Fetching data from deep object storage for every single read
Lack of pagination or size limits on text payloads
idealSolutionCharacteristics: Uses Object Storage or a NoSQL document store for persistent text blobs
Places a CDN or distributed cache in front to absorb read traffic spikes

questions.title: Page View Counter Service
questions.description: Design a high-throughput view counter for articles. The system must accept view events without blocking the user and eventually consistency is acceptable.
requirements: Aggregate counts accurately without losing events
expectedPatterns: Buffers write events asynchronously before applying them to the DB
antiPatterns: Executing SQL `UPDATE counter = counter + 1` for every single request directly
Locking database rows on every view event
idealSolutionCharacteristics: API pushes view events to a queue or distributed log (e.g., Kafka)
Background workers aggregate events (e.g., count per minute) and flush in batches to the database

questions.title: Feature Flag Management
questions.description: Design a configuration system that allows toggling features for specific users or global traffic. Flag evaluations happen extremely frequently and must not block main application flows.
requirements: Evaluate flags at 5000 requests per second
expectedPatterns: Caches flag rules directly in the application layer or nearest edge cache
antiPatterns: Making a network call to the database every time a feature flag is checked
Centralized monolithic configuration service with no failover
idealSolutionCharacteristics: Clients/Servers pull flag configurations and cache them in-memory
Uses a Pub/Sub mechanism to invalidate and refresh local caches when a flag is updated via the admin panel

questions.title: Single-Room Chat
questions.description: Design a backend for a single high-traffic chat room (like a livestream chat). Messages sent by one user must be broadcasted to all connected clients efficiently.
expectedPatterns: Uses a Pub/Sub mechanism to fan out messages across multiple gateway servers
Maintains long-lived connections horizontally
antiPatterns: Storing messages in DB and having clients constantly long-poll the database
A single server handling all WebSocket connections
idealSolutionCharacteristics: Client connects to stateful WebSocket Gateway servers via a Load Balancer
Gateways subscribe to a Redis Pub/Sub channel to receive messages and push to clients

questions.title: Scalable URL Shortener with Analytics
questions.description: Design a highly available URL shortener that not only redirects but also tracks detailed click analytics (geolocation, device type) at scale.
requirements: Ingest 10000 analytics events per second without slowing down redirects
expectedPatterns: Decouples read redirect path from write analytics path
Uses queues to buffer high-volume analytics data
antiPatterns: Performing synchronous database INSERTs for analytics on the redirect request thread
Relying on a single relational DB for both fast key-lookups and heavy OLAP queries
idealSolutionCharacteristics: Uses Cache (Redis) to serve redirects extremely fast
Redirect API drops an analytics event into a message broker (Kafka) asynchronously
Analytics workers consume events and batch insert into a data warehouse or NoSQL store

questions.title: Real-Time Chat System
questions.description: Design a multi-room, 1-on-1 real-time chat application (like WhatsApp/Discord). The architecture must handle user presence, message routing, and reliable delivery.
requirements: Process 20000 messages per second with cross-node routing
Latency from sender to receiver under 250ms
expectedPatterns: Routes messages between stateful gateway servers via a backend messaging bus
Caches presence state to avoid DB lookups on connection
antiPatterns: Broadcasting all messages to all servers rather than targeted routing
Using synchronous HTTP polling for a chat system at scale
idealSolutionCharacteristics: WebSocket servers hold connections; a Session Cache maps users to their active WebSocket server
Inbound messages are routed via Pub/Sub or a Message Broker directly to the recipient's connected server
Database is used asynchronously for message history and offline storage

questions.title: Social News Feed
questions.description: Design a social media news feed. The system must aggregate posts from followed users, supporting users with millions of followers without latency spikes.
requirements: Handle 10000 feed read requests per second
Support celebrity accounts with high fan-out load
expectedPatterns: Employs a hybrid fan-out model (push for regular users, pull for celebrities)
Precomputes timelines and stores them in a fast cache layer
antiPatterns: Executing a SQL JOIN across all followed users' posts on every feed read request
Synchronous fan-out for a user with 5 million followers blocking the post API
idealSolutionCharacteristics: Uses 'fan-out-on-write' via worker queues to pre-build news feeds in Redis for active users
Uses 'fan-out-on-read' for celebrity accounts to prevent massive queue backups
Merges cache data efficiently at read time

questions.title: Search Autocomplete Service
questions.description: Design a typeahead autocomplete system for a search engine. Queries must return suggestions instantly as the user types.
requirements: Update suggestions based on trending searches asynchronously
expectedPatterns: Uses highly optimized in-memory data structures (like Tries) distributed across nodes
Caches top prefixes heavily
antiPatterns: Executing `LIKE 'prefix%'` queries against a relational database per keystroke
Building the autocomplete index synchronously on user query paths
idealSolutionCharacteristics: Maintains an in-memory Trie data structure for fast prefix lookups
Background workers aggregate search logs via messaging queues to update Trie weights periodically
Edge caching / CDN caches the most popular prefixes (e.g., 'a', 'ap', 'app')

questions.title: Video Streaming Platform
questions.description: Design a video streaming platform like Netflix. The system must handle heavy outbound bandwidth for streaming and async processing for video transcoding.
requirements: Ensure low latency start times (under 500ms API response)
Process uploaded videos into multiple resolutions and bitrates
expectedPatterns: Relies heavily on CDNs for actual video chunk delivery
Decouples video upload from immediate availability via async processing
antiPatterns: Streaming raw video files directly from application servers
Processing video encoding on the same machines serving web traffic
idealSolutionCharacteristics: Web servers handle metadata, auth, and return CDN URLs for video manifests
Video files are split into chunks, transcoded by background worker clusters, and pushed to Object Storage/CDN
Uses Edge Caching aggressively to minimize origin fetches

questions.title: Real-Time Bidding Service
questions.description: Design an ad-tech Real-Time Bidding (RTB) engine. The system receives bid requests and must evaluate targets, run algorithms, and respond within a strict latency budget.
requirements: Evaluate thousands of active ad campaigns concurrently
expectedPatterns: Keeps campaign metadata and user segments entirely in fast memory/cache
Aggressively drops requests (timeouts) rather than queueing if latency budget is exceeded
antiPatterns: Querying disk-based relational DBs to check campaign budgets during an active bid
Garbage collection pauses causing missed bid deadlines
idealSolutionCharacteristics: Stores all active campaign and targeting rules in an in-memory database (e.g., Redis/Aerospike)
App servers process bid logic completely statelessly and scale horizontally
Asynchronously writes bid logs to a message queue for billing and analytics

questions.title: Global Ride-Sharing Platform
questions.description: Design the core routing and dispatch engine for a global ride-sharing service. The system must track high-frequency location updates from drivers and match them to riders spatially.
requirements: Match riders to drivers within 3 seconds
Maintain system availability across multiple regions
expectedPatterns: Uses geo-sharding (e.g., Geohash/S2 cells) to partition driver location data
Decouples location ingestion from complex matching algorithms via messaging
antiPatterns: Updating driver rows in a standard SQL DB for every GPS ping
Attempting global locking during a ride match
idealSolutionCharacteristics: Driver apps push location to an ingestion queue or memory store partitioned by Geohash
Dispatch workers subscribe to region-specific queues to compute nearest-neighbor matches
Uses WebSockets or Server-Sent Events to push match status back to clients

questions.title: Real-Time Fraud Detection Engine
questions.description: Design a real-time fraud detection engine for payment transactions. Every transaction must be scored against complex ML models and historical user profiles within milliseconds.
requirements: Hard latency limit: 200ms for scoring decision
Compute aggregations over moving time windows (e.g., spend in last 1hr)
expectedPatterns: Employs a fast in-memory Feature Store for user history lookups
Uses stream processing for continuous sliding window aggregations
antiPatterns: Executing complex SQL aggregations on the main transactional database synchronously
Loading ML models from disk on every scoring request
idealSolutionCharacteristics: API node queries a low-latency Feature Store (Redis) for pre-computed user aggregates
Applies pre-loaded ML models in memory for scoring
A parallel async stream processor (e.g., Flink) consumes the transaction log to continuously update the Feature Store aggregates

questions.title: HTAP Analytics Platform
questions.description: Design a Hybrid Transactional/Analytical Processing (HTAP) system. The platform must accept high-volume transactional writes while allowing heavy analytical queries on fresh data.
requirements: Handle 30000 writes/sec and 500 complex analytical queries/sec
Data must be available for analytics within 5 seconds of write
Analytical queries must not degrade transactional write performance
expectedPatterns: Separates Row-oriented transactional stores from Column-oriented analytical stores
Replicates data near real-time via Change Data Capture (CDC)
antiPatterns: Running analytical aggregates on the primary operational database
Using nightly ETL batches when 5-second freshness is required
idealSolutionCharacteristics: Writes land in a scalable row-store database (OLTP) optimized for fast inserts
A CDC pipeline (e.g., Debezium + Kafka) streams changes continuously
Changes are ingested into a columnar analytical database (OLAP) for fast aggregation queries

questions.title: Global Payments Ledger
questions.description: Design an immutable double-entry ledger system for a global payments processor. Consistency, fault tolerance, and absolute correctness are paramount.
requirements: Guarantee zero lost transactions and strict idempotency
expectedPatterns: Uses strict ACID-compliant databases for financial state
Implements distributed idempotency keys to prevent double-charging
Buffers ledger finalization via persistent queues
antiPatterns: Using eventual consistency (NoSQL) for core account balances
Processing financial transactions without idempotency constraints
idealSolutionCharacteristics: Synchronous API checks idempotency cache and reserves funds in the relational DB
API drops an event to a highly durable message bus (e.g., Kafka with strict acks)
Async workers securely append the double-entry records to the immutable ledger store

questions.title: Distributed Job Scheduler
questions.description: Design a distributed job scheduler that executes delayed and recurring tasks reliably at scale.
expectedPatterns: async_processing
antiPatterns: running jobs synchronously
idealSolutionCharacteristics: Uses message broker to queue scheduled jobs
Workers poll and execute jobs asynchronously

questions.title: Log Aggregation System
questions.description: Design a centralized logging system that collects and processes logs from distributed services.
expectedPatterns: async_processing
antiPatterns: direct DB writes from all services
idealSolutionCharacteristics: Uses broker to buffer logs
Processes logs asynchronously before storage

questions.title: File Upload Service
questions.description: Design a system to upload large files efficiently without blocking application servers.
expectedPatterns: async_processing
antiPatterns: processing uploads synchronously
idealSolutionCharacteristics: Uses async workers to process uploads
Stores metadata separately from files

questions.title: Leaderboard Service
questions.description: Design a real-time leaderboard system that ranks users based on scores.
expectedPatterns: caching
antiPatterns: sorting DB queries repeatedly
idealSolutionCharacteristics: Uses sorted sets in cache for ranking
Avoids DB queries for top results

questions.title: Metrics Monitoring System
questions.description: Design a monitoring system that tracks metrics and triggers alerts.
expectedPatterns: caching
antiPatterns: real-time DB aggregation
idealSolutionCharacteristics: Caches aggregated metrics
Uses efficient write path for ingestion

questions.title: Notification Preference Service
questions.description: Design a system to store and retrieve user notification preferences efficiently.
expectedPatterns: caching
antiPatterns: DB lookup per request
idealSolutionCharacteristics: Caches preferences in memory
Updates asynchronously

questions.title: URL Preview Generator
questions.description: Generate previews (title, image) for URLs asynchronously.
expectedPatterns: async_processing
antiPatterns: blocking HTTP scraping
idealSolutionCharacteristics: Uses workers to fetch metadata
Caches previews for reuse

questions.title: Search Ranking Service
questions.description: Rank search results based on relevance signals.
expectedPatterns: caching
antiPatterns: ranking in DB per request
idealSolutionCharacteristics: Precomputes ranking signals
Caches top results

questions.title: Session Store
questions.description: Design a distributed session store for web applications.
expectedPatterns: caching
antiPatterns: storing sessions in local memory
idealSolutionCharacteristics: Uses distributed cache for session storage
Replicates session data

questions.title: Webhook Delivery System
questions.description: Deliver webhooks reliably to third-party endpoints.
expectedPatterns: async_processing
antiPatterns: synchronous webhook calls
idealSolutionCharacteristics: Queues webhook events
Uses retry mechanism with backoff
